conclusion: C1 should be dropped: its central construct (task tolerance / spatial precision upgrade) was never defined consistently, its predictors are post-intervention, and n=5 tasks cannot support its multivariate held-out prediction. The prior round's broader claim that the direction has no researchable problem is also not supported: it conflated module-level saturation with mechanism-level resolution. The only residual question worth Gate A read-only verification is whether a state-level local spatial margin tau(s) and closed-loop gain g(s) predict when precision improvements change action outcomes; it is a HYPOTHESIS, not an experiment-ready project, and must beat analytic geometry, headroom, failure-mode proportion, crop augmentation and equal-budget test-time adaptation. No Gate B/C experiment is proposed or authorized.
